analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one troubleshooting row, near head line 2316. The row says a cold load can be refused with 503 or insufficient-memory when an idle model holds an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. It names ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel and autopilotHeldWeightBytes, and points to model-autopilot.md. The supplied base text (lines 1-801) does not include the changed region, so I reviewed the patch excerpt directly. No code, configuration, crypto, auth or trust-boundary change is made.

The documented behavior is an availability trade-off: held slots are excluded from eviction and get no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit. It touches no listed threat's assets, such as the A-001 prompt data or the T-041 prefix-cache surface. The base text I examined (Nemotron Super slot, prefix bank, KV admission, GLM5Next) is untouched context. I found nothing that invalidates a threat-model assumption.

I could not verify that the described Autopilot hold code exists, or whether holds can be abused for denial of service (T-010, T-029 style resource monopolization). Those would be a code-level concern for whichever PR introduced the hold logic. Integration should confirm the referenced symbols and the model-autopilot.md anchor are accurate. If Autopilot holds can be requested by an untrusted party, it may warrant a threat-model entry, but no evidence of that is supplied here.
